posts.text:
“Each week, ESPN's college football "insider," Heather Dinich, projects what the College Football Playoff rankings will look like.

This is what she said about Tennessee after the Vols' 27-13 win over LSU: 

"Beating an unranked, five-loss LSU team doesn't carry much weight, though the committee does reward teams for wins against opponents .500 or better."

The same writer after Alabama defeated LSU two weeks ago:

"Saturday's convincing win at LSU validated the committee's vote for Bama as its top two-loss team." 

The same writer after Texas defeated LSU last week: 

"The Longhorns have one of the best résumés in the country -- regardless of record -- with wins against Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri and now LSU."

In this week's analysis, Dinich said Tennessee is hurt by their lack of offensive production, citing the fact that the Vols were 4 of 17 on third down and had 308 yards of offense." 

But two weeks ago, when she was praising Alabama for its win over LSU, the Tide's offensive production was: 285 yards. 

I don't normally buy into the ESPN-hates-Tennessee dialogue. Most college football fans make similar claims, regardless of which team they root for. 

But in the case of Dinich, it's hard to ignore. 

Alabama being ranked several spots ahead of Tennessee despite the two teams having the same record and the Vols defeating Alabama 26-10 in their head-to-head matchup has been a point of major consternation for Tennessee fans, and deservedly so. 

Dinich doesn't actually get a say in the rankings, of course, but many believe that the CFP selection committee feeds information to ESPN (much like the NCAA Tournament selection committee in basketball has long been believed to feed insider intel to ESPN's Joe Lunardi). 

Even if she isn't privy to what the CFP committee is thinking, Dinich clearly has a deep-seated bias against Tennessee. 

This is what she said about Tennessee's No. 20 preseason ranking back in August: 

"I can’t believe Tennessee is even ranked. Why is Tennessee ranked, let alone at No. 20? I mean, they better find a quarterback and find some answers fast there. I have so many questions about them, not to say they can’t do it. Based on answers and not questions, I don’t know why the Vols are in there.”

And in 2024, when Tennessee finished the regular season with a 10-2 record, Dinich implied that three-loss Alabama should make the playoff field ahead of the Vols. 

Maybe Dinich has an ex who graduated from the University of Tennessee. Maybe she's related to Greg Schiano. Whatever the reason, this lady has hatred for Tennessee oozing out of everything she writes.”

~Ben Garrett, FB

posts.text:
I’ll never forget this.

I cooked for my boyfriend and after we finished eating, I gathered our dishes and was about to start washing them by the sink (I don’t have a dishwasher) when my boyfriend stopped me.

“No baby. You cooked this delicious meal for me, so I’ll be the one doing the dishes.”

I told him it was fine and that I was used to doing it myself, but he clearly wasn’t having it. Instead, he picked me up and carried me over to my bed. Carefully setting me down, he leaned towards me and said:

“You sit here, be pretty, play on your DS and let me handle the dishes okay?”

I was so flustered that all I could do was nod. He smiled, gave me a kiss and made his way back to the kitchen to do the dishes.

To be clear, much of what I said has been said by the leaders of other labs. What I *am* saying is this path is not inevitable.

I am saying leaders and leadership matter more than ever, and that’s why I’m proud of the work that Mark and I have done at Meta to put safety as a top focus of our efforts, including delaying the launch of Muse for months and being a leader on the SI Accords that all of our peers have signed onto.
